title: Human factual judgments improved after a matched AI debate
summary: Among 92 people who reconsidered the same factual item after reading both sides of a Claude Opus 4.5 debate, accuracy rose from 41.3% to 57.6%. The result concerns non-experts in one online study and a protocol that held the question’s subtopic fixed.

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 authors and affiliations, human protocols and model setup, and Table 5

evidence.tested: Table 5 reports paired pre/post accuracy for the same-subtopic protocol, with a 16.31 percentage-point change and a Holm-adjusted McNemar p-value of 0.028.
evidence.unknown: The paired change does not establish how the protocol compares with alternatives, which differed in what participants saw or judged. The study did not measure long-term retention or behavior.
evidence.ai_role: Claude Opus 4.5 generated the opposing sides of a same-subtopic debate before people re-answered the same factual item.
